intro: You are at the Miletus Museum, in Aydın province, opened in 1973. It gathers the finds of Miletus, Didyma and Priene, and in a single hall it lays out what a city managed to leave behind, even after all four of its harbours silted up.
history: The museum stands at the entrance to the Miletus site, beside the excavation house. Its collection covers Didyma and Priene as well as Miletus. And here is the twist: the harbours of all three silted up under the Meander, so finds from these port cities are now displayed kilometres inland.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Archaic sculpture, the Roman portraits, the finds from Didyma and the Byzantine-period works.
facts: Did you know? Miletus was the home of Hippodamus, who devised the grid city plan. The layout the museum explains is still the one most of the world's cities use, and after the Persians destroyed Miletus, the city was rebuilt to his design. The museum also holds the finds of Didyma and Priene alongside those of Miletus — and the harbours of all three were filled by silt from the Meander.
outro: This brings our tour of the Miletus Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These objects outlived their harbours; let them keep their story for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
